_schema.note: Canonical catalog for the commuting quiz (commute.html). Edit this file directly and push — GitHub Pages redeploys automatically. Optional live override: set SHEET_CSV_URL in commute.html to a published Google Sheet CSV with the same column names. Specs are researched from real current/recent models but are NOT live-verified against manufacturer spec sheets — treat as a well-informed prototype catalog, not a scraped, guaranteed-current source. An entry may carry an optional '_verified' field noting exactly which fields were confirmed against a live source, when, and where — absence of that field means the whole entry is knowledge-based, not scraped. See DATA.md for the catalog's scope and how to grow it responsibly.

fields.name: string — model name shown to users
fields.origin: string — country of the brand, used for the 'prefer Canadian' filter
fields.wheel: number — wheel diameter in mm (700 road/hybrid, 650/660 smaller hybrid, 406 folding ~20in)
fields.minH: number — cm, lower bound of rider height this bike fits
fields.maxH: number — cm, upper bound of rider height this bike fits
fields.price: number — face-value price in whatever 'currency' says; the budget slider compares this number as-is and does not convert between currencies
fields.currency: optional string, 3-letter code (e.g. 'CAD') — omit to mean USD, the default for every entry added before this field existed
fields.cargoCapacity: number 0-3 — 0 none, 1 rack-ready, 2 rack+panniers, 3 heavy-duty cargo
fields.weight: number — kg, used to score portability/storage importance
fields.foldable: boolean — true only for actual folding-frame bikes; weighted heavily for portability since folding matters more than a kg or two of weight
fields.maxComfortDistance: number — km, comfortable one-way commute distance
fields.groupset: string — the actual drivetrain/hub name shown to users; matched against the groupset-preference question by manufacturer keyword or by gearing==='internal' for 'low-maintenance'
fields.colors: array of strings — color options this model actually ships in
fields.ridingPosition: 'upright' | 'relaxed' | 'sporty' — how far forward you lean; translates handlebar/geometry style into a plain-language question
fields.fendersIncluded: boolean — ships with fenders/mudguards standard (not just fender mounts)
fields.tireProfile: 'standard' | 'wide' — wide covers gravel/adventure and semi-fat e-bike tires, matched against the flat-tire-worry question
fields.suspensionFork: boolean — has a front suspension fork for rough pavement/potholes
fields.image: string — relative path (e.g. images/commute/trek-fx2.jpg) or full URL to a product photo; leave empty to show the sketch placeholder
fields.retailerUrl: optional string — a specific product page URL, set ONLY when a human has actually opened that exact URL and confirmed it shows this bike (e.g. a page the user shared). Never guessed or constructed. When absent, the result card links to a live web search for the bike's name instead of a specific (possibly wrong or dead) product page — price/stock are the least stable part of any catalog entry, so we point to a live source rather than caching a number that will go stale.

bikes.name: Priority Continuum Onyx
bikes._verified: IMPORTANT CORRECTION: this bike was miscategorized as powerType 'ebike' at $2,999 — it is actually a pedal-only bike with no motor or battery, confirmed directly at prioritybicycles.com on 2026-09-09 ('the all-season, ready-out-of-the-box, belt drive commuter and touring bicycle', Enviolo CVT hub + Gates Carbon Drive belt, no electric assist mentioned anywhere). Corrected powerType to 'pedal', price to $1,349 (real MSRP), weight to 14kg (31lb, was an inflated 22kg consistent with an e-bike), and type from 'hilly_assist' (implies e-assist) to 'city_streets'. This was a real scoring bug: a rider who asked for e-assist could have been shown a non-motorized bike as a top match. Product photo from prioritybicycles.com.
